main_text.l: AD IOANNEM IACOMOTVM GENEVENSIS ECCLESIÆ ministrum oda Henrici Altenhouij.

VALI ruina strauerit inclytas Arces Sionis, & Moriæ decus Turpârit, excelsam nefando Rex Solymam populatus igni: Cum rege regnum, cum populo patres, Et cum sacrato Pontifices grege, Matres, catenatamque ducens Cum nuribus Babylona turbam: Flet luctuosis Helciades modis, Modum querelis ponere nescius Ruêtante lapsis ꝟsque rebus Corde feros super eiulatus. Tu molliori consocias lyrę Lugubre vates carmen Anathoti. Tendisque Lesboum seueris, Iane, sonis, Iacomote, plectrum. Qui lacrymarum flumina tanta, quis Lacus perenni fonte cadentibus Corriuet vndis, vt ruinam, & Perpetuæ mala seruitutis

page.notes: The verse is set with the first letter of "VALI" as a large woodcut initial "U" (decorated frame at left); transcribed as "VALI" joined to it. Line "Ruêtante" is printed as such in the scan; the word "Ructante" is doubtful and may be a misprint for "Ructante"; marked as printed. The line "Qui lacrymarum flumina tanta, quis" and the following lines are set as verse lines; they were run together in the transcription as one paragraph because the printer's line breaks are not indented, so the stanza is one block. The stars "* *" and page number "4" appear at the foot of the text block; the stars are a signature-like mark and are not a catchword, so they are not transcribed. Show-through from the reverse page is present in the right margin and was left out.
